[[Norcross, Georgia|Norcross]], Georgia | career_highlights = | honors = | records = | tournaments = | tournament_list = }} '''Gani Oladimeji Lawal, Jr.''' (born November 7, 1988 in [[College Park, Georgia|College Park]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]) is an [[Nigerian American]] [[college basketball]] player with the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team]]. A junior, Lawal led the team in field-goal percentage and blocked shots in 2007–2008.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1406628 Gani Lawal Profile] at scout.com. Currently, Lawal is expected to be a late first round pick in the 2010 NBA Draft.[http://spoonhoops.com/2010-Mock-Draft.php] at spoonhoops.com During his time at [[Norcross High School]], Lawal was named to the [[McDonald's All-American Team]] following his senior season and was Mr. Basketball 2007 in Georgia.[http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lawal_gani00.html Profile] at RamblinWreck.com After originally entering the draft following his Sophomore year, Lawal pulled out of the draft on June 14, 2009 to return to Georgia Tech for his junior year.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4257782] ==2007–08== In his freshman season of 2007–08, Lawal scored 10 points on 5-of-6 shots, with four rebounds at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], snapping a streak of six games in single digits. He also had a game-high nine rebounds in a 77–64 win over [[Presbyterian College|Presbyterian]] on January 6, 2008.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280060059 Georgia Tech 77, Presbyterian 64 – Recap] ==2008–09== In his sophomore season of 2008–09, Lawal scored a career-best 34 points[http://www.wtopnews.com/?nid=210&sid=1540255 Georgia Tech beats Vanderbilt 63–51] in an 85–83 Georgia Tech loss to [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] on December 3, 2008.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=283380059 Penn State 85, Georgia Tech 83 – Box score] He had a career-high 16 rebounds in a 63–58 win over [[Tennessee State University|Tennessee State]] on December 30, 2008.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283650059 Georgia Tech 63, Tennessee St. 58 – Recap] He bettered that mark by one rebound when he pulled down 17 in a 70–56 home loss to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] on January 14, 2009.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290140059 Singler, Henderson stabilize No. 2 Duke against careless Georgia Tech] ==Personal== Lawal's mother's name is Michelle, and his father, Gani, Sr., a real estate and mortgage broker, is from Nigeria.
